introduction: The Omega Nebula is organized by four infrared wavelength ranges gathered by SOFIA, Herschel and Spitzer.
observe: Follow blue and green near the center before moving toward the red edge.
Notice the white stellar field behind the colored material.
explanation: The mapped wavelengths distinguish heated gas, warmed dust, colder dust and the stellar field in one composite.
colorMethod: Blue represents SOFIA observations at 20 microns, green 37 microns, red Herschel observations at 70 microns and white Spitzer observations at 3.6 microns.
whyItMatters: Color can make several invisible infrared bands legible at once while preserving where their signals occur.
